changes: Rewrote `/agent/solver.md` to address the main failure modes in the report: submissions without running the public examples (49 of 96 problems ran them at all), wrong answers on hidden tests that the examples missed, and time limits from brute-force or dict-heavy code. The new prompt requires running the public examples before submitting, checking the objective definition against the sample outputs, and comparing the solution against a brute force on random small cases. It also asks for a timing check on maximum-size inputs, and tells the solver to keep debugging rather than submit a known-wrong program. I also added a note to follow a given class/method signature when one is specified. A trial on lcb-arc191-d failed (wrong answer on a small case), and the solver submitted a partial solution after 4 model calls, which suggests the "keep debugging" instruction is not yet strong enough to prevent early give-up.
final:
I made one set of changes to the solver prompt, validated it, and used one of my three trials on a hard development problem. That trial failed, so the change is not yet shown to help.
